subsystems.name: Interstellar propulsion
subsystems.role: gets a payload to another star in centuries, not millennia — typically aiming for a few per cent of light speed or more.

subsystems.name: Seed payload
subsystems.role: the minimum needed to start a colony: genetic material, embryos or people, plus the tools to build everything else.

subsystems.name: In-situ resource use
subsystems.role: the colony must live off the destination system rather than Earth.

subsystems.name: Communications and navigation
subsystems.role: keeps a settled system linked to its parents across light-years.

subsystems.name: Replication and launch loop
subsystems.role: a settled system must build its own ships to send onward — this is what turns single missions into a wave.

buildSteps.title: Solve cheap access to orbit
buildSteps.detail: A planetary civilisation first needs routine, low-cost access to space so that building large ships becomes affordable.

buildSteps.title: Build off-world industry
buildSteps.detail: Mining, refining and manufacturing move off the home planet to use asteroid and lunar material instead of lifting everything from the surface.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate interstellar propulsion
buildSteps.detail: A drive concept is tested at small scale: fusion-pulse designs such as those studied under Project Daedalus, or laser-pushed lightsails as in the Breakthrough Starshot concept.

buildSteps.title: Send robotic precursors
buildSteps.detail: Uncrewed probes travel to a nearby star, decelerate or fly by, and report back what is actually there.

buildSteps.title: Establish a first outpost
buildSteps.detail: A crewed or fully automated settlement lands, builds habitats and begins using local water, metals and volatiles.

buildSteps.title: Reach self-sufficiency
buildSteps.detail: The outpost grows enough food, energy and equipment to survive and reproduce without resupply from home.

buildSteps.title: Build the next ships
buildSteps.detail: With surplus capacity, the settlement constructs its own interstellar vessels — the step that makes expansion a wave rather than a one-off voyage.

buildSteps.title: Repeat across the galaxy
buildSteps.detail: Each new system repeats the process; at one per cent of light speed and a new star every few centuries, the wave needs millions of years to cross the galaxy.

prerequisites.tech: Interstellar propulsion at a few per cent of light speed
prerequisites.why: no drive has been demonstrated beyond paper studies and small laboratory tests.

prerequisites.tech: Closed-loop life support and in-situ resource use
prerequisites.why: spacecraft and the ISS recycle air and water, and Mars missions have demonstrated making oxygen from local material, but not full self-sufficiency.
automated factories exist on Earth, but nothing that could build a starship without human supply chains.
fission reactors have flown and fusion reactors are still experimental.

prerequisites.tech: Long-term human health and reproduction off Earth
prerequisites.why: no mammal has been shown to reproduce healthily across generations in space or on another world.

pathway.milestone: robotic interstellar probe concepts and sail experiments
pathway.unlocks: real data on whether the nearest exoplanets are reachable targets.

pathway.milestone: a probe reaches another star system and returns data
pathway.unlocks: confirmation that interstellar flight is possible at all.

pathway.milestone: a self-sufficient settlement on another world or moon in our own system
pathway.unlocks: the industrial base and life-support know-how for interstellar colonisation.

pathway.milestone: a crewed or automated settlement around another star that can build its own ships
pathway.unlocks: the start of a genuine galactic wave.

pathway.milestone: settlement spreading through the galaxy over millions of years
pathway.unlocks: either a detectable galactic civilisation — or, if we still see nothing, sharper constraints on the Fermi paradox.
